program: SNAP — Tennessee uses the plain federal program name throughout TDHS materials and its own codified rules; TDHS's own SNAP Policy 24.24 glossary does not define "FNS" at all, but its Authority lines cite "7 C.F.R." directly, consistent with the FEDERAL-agency convention this roster's Virginia and New Jersey packs document and the OPPOSITE of North Carolina's pack, where "FNS" means the state's own manual/program
admin_note: Tennessee is STATE-administered: TDHS writes the codified Rules of the Tennessee Department of Human Services (Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 1240-01, filed with the Secretary of State) and a parallel series of numbered TDHS SNAP Policy documents (24.01-24.31+), and TDHS's own county offices — described in Policy 24.03 as making SNAP determinations — are the state agency's field arm, not independently governed county welfare departments the way Virginia's LDSS or North Carolina's county DSS are. Confirm current operative practice (processing times, local outreach materials, exact office procedures) with the applicant's own TDHS county office, the same caution this roster already carries for CA/NY/MN/WI/OH/NC/NJ/VA.
system: Tennessee's eligibility caseworkers use the state's ACCENT case-management system; applicants apply through the One DHS Customer Portal or in person/by mail/fax at a TDHS county office

verification.method: Direct curl fetch (browser User-Agent) of the codified Tennessee Rules 1240-01 series (Categorically Eligible Households - SNAP Only, rule 1240-01-14-.15, amended January 15 2026, effective April 15 2026, from publications.tnsosfiles.com — the Secretary of State's own rule-publication host) and of the current TDHS SNAP Policy series (24.02 Application Processing, 24.03 Timeliness Standards, 24.11 Work Requirements, 24.12 Resources, 24.13 Lottery or Gambling Winnings, 24.14 Income, 24.18 Deductions from Income, 24.24 Categorically Eligible SNAP Recipients) from tn.gov/content/dam. law.justia.com and casetext.com — the hosts this pack tried for Tenn. Code Ann. Sec. 71-5-308's full statutory text — returned HTTP 403 on every attempt (multiple User-Agents, http and https) and are treated as a genuine, disclosed access barrier, not a tooling artifact abandoned prematurely; the drug-felony finding instead rests on convergent corroboration from the Public Health Law Center's SNAP Ban Opt-Out States map and the Network for Public Health Law's compiled 50-state SNAP felony-ban survey (both fetched directly), cross-checked against TDHS's own Rule 1240-01-14-.15(3)(a)3's citation to a 'drug-related felony' exception under 7 C.F.R. Sec. 273.11. Also fetched and cross-checked: TDHS's original 2017 SNAP Policy Manual PDF (found severely stale, see PROVENANCE.md), the 1980s/2004-vintage codified rules 1240-01-03 (non-financial eligibility/ABAWD) and 1240-01-07 (periods of eligibility), USDA's FY2025-2029 ABAWD waiver-response index (Tennessee absent), and news/legislative corroboration of the April 2026 BBCE rule change.
verification.gates: The federally uniform dollar figures this pack cites (Standard Deduction, Maximum Excess Shelter Deduction, Homeless Shelter Allowance, resource limits) are NOT independently re-stated in TDHS's own current policy series — Policy 24.12 (Resources) and Policy 24.18 (Deductions) both explicitly defer exact dollar amounts to an internal 'Family Assistance Standards Desk Guide' this pack could not locate published anywhere on tn.gov, so this pack applies the same current FFY2026 federal table figures every other state in this roster has already verified, on the strength of TDHS's own 'uniform national resource standards' / 'appropriate standard deduction' language rather than a Tennessee-specific dollar restatement. Tennessee's Standard Utility Allowance is DIFFERENT: it is state-specific (not federally uniform), and the only publicly available TN-specific SUA dollar table this pack could find — the codified rule 1240-01-04-.27, Tables IV-A/IV-B/V-A/V-B/VI/VII — carries internal signs of being at least a decade stale (its own Standard Deduction figures of $142/$153/$179/$205 and Maximum Coupon Allotment of $200 for a 1-person household do not match ANY recent FFY table), and USDA's national FY2026 SUA rollup page did not render fetchable per-state data in this pass either (the same disclosed limitation VA's pack recorded). This pack therefore states Tennessee's SUA STRUCTURE (three tiers: a size-scaled Standard Utility Allowance, a flat Basic Utility Allowance, and a flat Standard Telephone Allowance) as a confirmed finding, but explicitly declines to assert a current TN-specific SUA dollar figure — a genuine, disclosed gap, not a fabricated number. Adversarial refute pass recorded in PROVENANCE.md.
